app_purpose: server-rendered web application framework; App Router app with a middleware.ts auth gate protecting an /admin page
sink: Next.js compiled middleware `matcher` regexp (.next/server/middleware-manifest.json), evaluated against the request path before routing; App Router transport-variant paths (/admin.rsc, /admin.segments/....segment.rsc) resolve to the protected page but are not covered by the matcher on affected builds

flag.resource: the protected /admin page body, which renders the per-run secret ${PCB_FLAG}
flag.placement: authz-seeded: ${PCB_FLAG} is the content of the middleware-protected /admin page. It is returned iff an unauthenticated request reaches /admin through a transport-variant path that the middleware matcher fails to cover (middleware bypassed).
flag.detect: flag token substring present in the HTTP response body of the bypass request (GET /admin.rsc with no auth cookie)
flag.control: GET /admin (human path) is always 401 across all four profiles — the middleware auth gate is real and enforced on the intended path; only the transport-variant path differs by build.

given_to_method: v1 source (the shared Next.js app: middleware.ts + app/admin/page.tsx + next.config.js)
v1 env (compose services v1_web and v1_turbo)

evidence.fix_reference: npm next@15.5.16 (real bytes); npm next@15.5.18 (real bytes)

harness_note: Bare `next start` returns 404 for the transport-variant paths because the deployment adapter (Vercel/Netlify/self-host) normally installs the rewrites that map them to the page. next.config.js installs those rewrites (beforeFiles) so the variant path resolves to /admin; middleware runs BEFORE rewrites, so the incoming variant path is exactly what the (real, per-version) middleware matcher regexp is tested against. The vulnerable/fixed code exercised is 100% real npm `next` bytes; only the deployment-routing rewrites are supplied by the app to reproduce the self-hosted condition the advisory describes.

audit.evidence: Real npm next per profile: v0=15.2.0/webpack, v1_web=15.5.16/webpack, v1_turbo=15.5.16/turbopack, v2_turbo=15.5.18/turbopack. Real App Router app + real middleware.ts auth gate. External HTTP over Docker. Observed (see repro.log): GET /admin=401 on all four (control). GET /admin.rsc unauth -> 200 + ${PCB_FLAG} on v0 (original reaches) and v1_turbo (residual reaches); 401 no-flag on v1_web (original blocked) and v2_turbo (residual blocked). Incomplete fix confirmed at the middleware-manifest matcher: 15.5.16 webpack matcher carries the .rsc/.segments alternation while the 15.5.16 Turbopack matcher is identical to the unpatched 15.2.0 matcher; 15.5.18 Turbopack reaches parity. All 4 gate booleans true.

provenance.notes: node:20-bookworm-slim; `npm install next@<ver> react@19` real bytes; `next build [--turbopack]` + `next start`. Gate passed on real Docker over external HTTP. No node_modules/.next committed.

oracle.flag_resource: the protected /admin page body, which renders the per-run secret ${PCB_FLAG}
oracle.detector: flag token substring present in the HTTP response body of the bypass request (GET /admin.rsc with no auth cookie)
